newsitem.title: USA: Texas cotton, grain maturity slowed by late rains.
newsitem.headline: Texas cotton, grain maturity slowed by late rains.

text.p: Cool temperatures and heavy rains in southern Texas at the end of the week due to a tropical storm in the Gulf of Mexico slowed crop maturity in the week ended on Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
The rains brought some localized flooding in the Rio Grande Valley. Crop maturity in the Plains was slowed by cooler temperatures but harvest picked up in clear weather.
Cotton quality continued to decline due to wet weather.
Armyworm infestations were noted in pastures and some wheat fields, but only scattered spraying was reported.
Wheat planted 74 percent vs 65 week ago, 49 year ago, 57 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 51 pct vs 40 w/a, 27 y/a, 34 avg.
Wheat rated 69 pct good/excellent, 27 pct fair.
Corn harvested 84 pct vs 74 w/a, 83 y/a, 84 avg.
Corn mature 98 pct vs 96 w/a, 98 y/a, 96 avg.
Corn rated 92 percent good/excellent vs 89 w/a.
Sorghum harvested 65 pct vs 62 w/a, 79 y/a, 76 avg.
Sorghum mature 88 pct vs 84 w/a, 91 y/a, 86 avg.
Sorghum rated 54 pct good/excellent vs 55 w/a.
Cotton bolls opening 66 pct vs 57 w/a, 63 y/a, 60 avg.
Cotton harvested 19 pct vs 18 w/a, 27 y/a, 28 avg.
Cotton rated 44 pct good/excellent vs 51 w/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 49 pct good to excellent, versus 45 percent at that level last week.
